key_insight: A low-resource LR-QAOA benchmark can mimic QEC syndrome-extraction behavior and turn the decay of an algorithmic signal into an effective hardware error metric.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware teams a practical way to compare quantum processors and QEC implementations, including mid-circuit measurement, reset, feed-forward, and scheduling, before running full logical-memory experiments.
method: Construct QAOA circuits from a code’s check structure to reproduce QEC-like connectivity and measurement patterns.
Run linear-parameter LR-QAOA with mid-circuit measurement to obtain an approximation ratio r as the benchmark signal.
Fit the decay of r versus depth to estimate an equivalent two-qubit depolarizing rate λ_eff.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated 10 QPUs from IBM, IQM, and Quantinuum, including circuits with up to 2950 MCM operations and code-structured runs up to 81, 91, and 48 data qubits on Quantinuum hardware.
watch_item: Because the benchmark maps algorithmic decay to an equivalent depolarizing rate, the interpretation may depend on code choice, compilation, and hardware-specific control errors rather than QEC primitives alone.
paper_title: Evaluating the performance of QEC primitives on quantum processors at large width and depth
